mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which increases corporate costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with sustained HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the previous quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5%.
